function.name: ThinQ_Connect
function.description: Send a command to control an appliance, such as setting operation modes, air flow strength, and target temperatures. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

body.description: A dictionary containing various control parameters for the appliance.

currentJobMode.description: The current mode of operation for the air conditioner.

windStrength.description: The strength level of the airflow.

monitoringEnabled.description: Flag to enable or disable air quality sensor monitoring.

airCleanOperationMode.description: The operation mode for the air cleaning process.

airConOperationMode.description: The operation mode for turning the air conditioner on or off.

powerSaveEnabled.description: Flag to enable or disable power-saving mode.

coolTargetTemperature.description: The target temperature for cooling mode in degrees Celsius. Value must be between 18 and 30.

targetTemperature.description: The general target temperature in degrees Celsius. Value must be between 18 and 30.

We need to interpret what they want. Possibly they want us to confirm that we turned it on? Or maybe they want us to turn it on? The phrase "the air conditioner turned on with cool mode." could be a statement. Maybe they want us to set the AC to cool mode. But they said "turned on with cool mode." That implies it's already on. But maybe they want us to ensure it's on. Let's interpret as they want us to set it to cool mode. So we should call the function to set currentJobMode to COOL, airConOperationMode to POWER_ON. Also maybe set targetTemperature to default 22. And maybe set other defaults.

We can call ThinQ_Connect with body: {currentJobMode:"COOL", airConOperationMode:"POWER_ON"}.

But we also need to consider that the user might want us to confirm. The instruction says: "When you do not know how to respond, ask clarifying questions." But we can respond with a confirmation. But we can also call the function. The best approach: respond with a short acknowledgement and then call the function. According to guidelines: "If you are going to use a function, you should first provide a brief explanation of your intent before calling the function." So we should say something like "Sure, I'll set the AC to cool mode and turn it on." Then call the function.

Thus we produce a response: "Sure, setting the AC to cool mode and turning it on." Then call the function with body: {currentJobMode:"COOL", airConOperationMode:"POWER_ON"}.

We don't need to specify windStrength etc unless needed. We'll just set those two. The function will return some result. We'll output that.
